Evelyn / Marissa —

Technical summary and constraints:

1) Anchored residency: Our control plane and customer tenancy can be configured to place model-serving instances and persistent storage (object and block) in an EU region (we typically provision eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). For normal traffic the inference execution path and data persistence remain in-region.

2) Transient cross-region processing: There are three scenarios where data may process outside the anchor region for short periods:
  - Failover / cold-start warmup (KV cache priming and model shard synchronization) — brief cross-region communication may occur to fetch model artifacts or warm caches.
  - Hot-replication for throughput spikes when dedicated capacity in-region is saturated and burst capacity is routed from a neighboring region.
  - Emergency routing for operator-triggered remediation (rare, manually approved).

In practice we can cap any such processing to an operational window. Based on current runtime behavior: typical transient hops are 0-6 hours for cache priming, and in exceptional burst/failover cases we see up to 24-48 hours while checkpoints and KV stores rehydrate. A 72-hour claim would be defensible only in the most extreme disaster-recovery scenarios and would need an explicit contractual exception and runbook.

3) Mitigations & controls we can provide now:
  - Region-bound KMS keys (customer-managed where required) to prevent decrypted material from leaving the region.
  - Audit traces for cross-region egress events with timestamps and request ids (we can surface a sample audit bundle).
  - Configurable ephemeral-hop window (we can set a customer policy to 0, 24, or 48 hours) and automated alerts when the window is exceeded.
  - Subprocessor activation windows: we can mark certain subprocessors as "active only for replication/failover" and provide activation timestamps in the roster.

Attachments: ops_runbook_transient-hop.md (ops runbook stub describing manual approvals and failover thresholds).

Recommendation: offer an EU-anchored residency commitment with a maximum ephemeral-hop window of 48 hours as our standard enterprise option; allow custom exceptions under an addendum for 72h disaster scenarios.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Reliability

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the questionnaire — good set of asks. We can provide an EU-anchored residency commitment for processing and storage, plus a defined, auditable policy for any transient cross-region processing. Summary below and I've attached the DPA redline and our current subprocessor roster for your review.

Summary commitment (proposed):
- Primary residency: Customer data at-rest and primary inference execution will be anchored to an EU region (you can pick eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
- Ephemeral-hop window: Redwood will not perform cross-region processing for longer than 48 hours except under a documented disaster-recovery addendum. Any event exceeding 48 hours will trigger immediate notification to MedicaHealth and escalation to our Security & Legal teams.
- Controls: region-bound CMKs (customer-managed option), per-request audit logs with timestamps and region metadata, and subprocessor activation timestamps (attached).

Attachments included: DPA_redline_v1.docx (highlighted language for ephemeral-hop and notification clauses), subprocessor_roster_20270416.csv (roles/purposes and activation windows), ops_runbook_transient-hop.md (operational steps and approval workflow).

Next steps:
1) Review the DPA redline and let us know if you'd like a follow-up call with Legal (Marissa can join).
2) If the 48-hour window is acceptable, we can provide a short contract addendum and a sample audit bundle for your review.

Happy to jump on a 30-min slot — proposed times: Tue Apr 20 10:00-10:30 CEST or Wed Apr 21 14:00-14:30 CEST.
